briefings.title: ETF Edge on Roundhill's Memory ETF surpassing $6 billion in record time

people.name: Drew Pettit
people.role: Research Director of U.S. Equity Strategy and ETF Strategy, Citi

briefings.tldr: The AI build-out has shifted memory chips (DRAM) from a cyclical consumer commodity to a critical data center bottleneck, driving massive earnings momentum and the record-breaking success of targeted semiconductor ETFs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The AI build-out has shifted memory chips (DRAM) from a cyclical consumer commodity to a critical data center bottleneck, driving massive earnings momentum and the record-breaking success of targeted semiconductor ETFs.

## The Evolution of the Memory Chip Market
* **AI as the Primary Bottleneck:** Memory chips have replaced processing power as the chief constraint in AI infrastructure. This supply-demand imbalance is projected to persist through 2026, and potentially as late as 2028, due to the 3-5 year lead time required to build new fabrication plants.
* **Structural Shift in Demand:**
    * **Micron Case Study:** Historically, data centers accounted for only 15% of Micron's business; today, that figure has reached 65%.
    * **Reduced Cyclicality:** The industry is moving away from short-term consumer contracts (TVs, phones) toward long-term data center contracts, making earnings more stable for leaders like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.
* **ETF Performance:** The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) has become one of the most successful launches in history, recently gaining 13% in a single session while broader indices remained flat.

## Valuation and Momentum Strategy
* **Earnings-Backed Growth:** Citi Research notes that while semi stocks have seen triple-digit price increases, they are supported by "up and to the right" earnings revisions.
    * **Example:** Micron alone added five dollars to S&P 500 earnings expectations this year.
* **Reasonable Multiples:** Despite 300% price moves, stocks remain "reasonably priced" because earnings expectations have increased six-to-eightfold.
* **Geopolitical Positioning:** 
    * **Emerging Markets:** Investors are looking to South Korea (KOSPI) and Taiwan for direct memory exposure.
    * **Tail Risk Hedging:** Large-cap U.S. growth acts as a "defensive" trade against higher oil prices and geopolitical conflict because "mega-cap tech runs on chips, not oil."

## The "AI Value Chain" and Next-Phase Enablers
* **Infrastructure Enablers:** Beyond chips, the build-out requires industrial names providing concrete, plumbing, and electrical work for data centers. These companies currently hold significant pricing power.
* **Optical/Photonics Bottlenecks:** Companies like Credo, Coherent, and Lumentum are essential for allowing high-speed chips to communicate with one another.
* **Bottleneck Trades:** Roundhill’s Generative AI ETF (CHAT) focuses on these "bottleneck" companies, as the connectivity and cooling infrastructure for new chips like Nvidia’s Blackwell and Vera Rubin are as critical as the processors themselves.

## Prediction Markets: The Next ETF Frontier
* **Event Contracts:** Roundhill is one of three firms with SEC applications for Prediction Market ETFs, which would allow investors to trade on political outcomes (e.g., House/Senate control or the Presidential election).
* **Portfolio Utility:**
    * **Direct Hedging:** These products offer a direct way to hedge portfolios against specific political or macro risks (like recessions) rather than using proxy baskets of stocks.
    * **Uncorrelated Assets:** These tools fit into the 2-5% "uncorrelated strategy" sleeve of modern portfolios, providing risk diversification that traditional markets cannot offer.
* **Regulatory Delays:** While the SEC has postponed decisions on these filings, proponents argue these markets are not novel, citing long-standing academic markets like the University of Iowa's.

> "Investors are waking up to the fact that the biggest bottleneck in the AI build-out is actually memory chips... We expect that the momentum for these names will continue because the demand is going to hold up." — **Dave Mazza**

> "We don't like price momentum unless it has earnings momentum and improvement, and the DRAM and semi stocks have that... even if we're up 300%, if your earnings expectations are up six to eightfold for the next few years, it still comes back reasonably priced." — **Drew Pettit**

> "Large-cap growth in the United States... is our favorite geopolitical hedge right now. You're relatively insulated versus the rest of the world. Mega-cap tech runs on chips, it doesn't run on oil." — **Drew Pettit**

briefings.title: Episode 53: Christian Angermayer - Founder of Apeiron Investment Group
briefings.tldr: Christian Angermayer, billionaire founder of Apeiron Investment Group, argues that long-term success is driven by "blissful ignorance," maintaining neuroplasticity, and making high-conviction, contrarian bets on the future of human health—specifically through the medicalization of psychedelics and performance-enhancing drugs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Christian Angermayer, billionaire founder of Apeiron Investment Group, argues that long-term success is driven by "blissful ignorance," maintaining neuroplasticity, and making high-conviction, contrarian bets on the future of human health—specifically through the medicalization of psychedelics and performance-enhancing drugs.

## The Path from Rural Bavaria to Multi-Millionaire at 25
*   **Early Ambition:** Raised in a small Bavarian village with no entrepreneurial role models, Angermayer started a tutoring business at 14 and was writing invoices as soon as he learned to write.
*   **Ribopharma & Alnylam:** 
    *   At age 20, he dropped out of university to co-found Ribopharma with his tutors, focusing on groundbreaking RNA interference (RNAi) technology. 
    *   The company merged with Alnylam Pharmaceuticals and went public via a SPAC in 2004.
    *   **Financial Exit:** By age 25, Angermayer was a multi-millionaire, but rejected the European tendency toward early retirement in favor of continuous "novelty seeking."
*   **Apeiron Investment Group:** Now manages over $7 billion, operating as a family office, a fund sponsor, and a "venture builder" that starts companies around unique, non-derivative ideas.

## The Psychedelic Renaissance: Compass Pathways and atai Life Sciences
*   **The Spiritual Catalysts:** Angermayer’s first psilocybin trip in 2014 convinced him that psychedelics show individuals "who they really are" rather than changing their personality. 
*   **The Novogratz Connection:** In 2017, following a "message" from a psychedelic trip to discuss mushrooms in every meeting, Angermayer pitched the idea to Mike Novogratz. The next morning, Novogratz’s sister called him about two entrepreneurs in Bali (the future founders of Compass Pathways) looking for funding for a mushroom company.
*   **Medicalization Strategy:** 
    *   **atai Life Sciences:** Founded to bring psychedelic compounds into mainstream psychiatry, taking it public at a $3.2 billion valuation.
    *   **Medical Framework:** Angermayer strictly opposes recreational use, advocating for clinicians to administer compounds under medical guidance, noting that the brain is not fully formed until age 21–22.

## The Enhanced Games: Disrupting the Olympic Model
*   **Contrarian Vision:** Angermayer backed Aron D’Souza’s "Enhanced Games" after almost every other investor declined. He views it as a necessary alternative to the "hypocritical" Olympics, where an estimated 44% of athletes use banned substances.
*   **Performance Medicine:** 
    *   **Recovery Focus:** The Games aim to prove that performance-enhancing drugs (PEDs) are primarily useful for helping the body recover from the "unnatural destruction" caused by elite sports, rather than just building muscle.
    *   **Transparency:** All participants must use medications under a doctor's supervision and obtain them through pharmacies, aligning with FDA standards.
*   **Public Market Debut:** The venture recently debuted as a performance medicine business on the NYSE at an over $1 billion market cap.

## Optimization, Longevity, and Success Mindset
*   **Personal Health Stack:**
    *   **Hormone Therapy:** Angermayer has used Testosterone Replacement Therapy (TRT) since age 30 (currently 250mg/week) to maintain his biological baseline.
    *   **Substance Avoidance:** He labels alcohol "pure poison" and warns that marijuana makes users "dumber and slower" scientifically. 
*   **Maintaining the "Young" Brain:** 
    *   **Neuroplasticity:** Success requires marrying experience with the "blissful ignorance" and creativity of youth. He uses psychedelics specifically to prevent the brain from becoming "rigid" with age.
    *   **Investment Intuition:** He describes himself as a "gut-feeling driven person" who relies on serendipity and the law of attraction.
*   **Universal Advice:** Angermayer recommends Napoleon Hill’s *Think and Grow Rich* as the foundational text for any aspiring entrepreneur, emphasizing that the "how" of manifesting success is less important than the fact that the principles work.

> "Every single big success I had, had I known all the problems which will come my way, I would never have done it. I would sit there like, 'Oh my God, no.' You need that kind of blissful ignorance." — **Christian Angermayer**

> "Psychedelics 100% mean... they do not change you, but what they do is show you who you really are." — **Christian Angermayer**

> "Aging sucks. I want to get wiser, but I want to look like I’m in my 20s, feel like I’m in my 20s, and have sex like I’m in my 20s." — **Christian Angermayer**

briefings.title: FICO’s Monopoly is Fading & Consumers Are the Winners w/ Kelsey Zhu | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 59
briefings.tldr: FICO’s aggressive price hikes—increasing mortgage credit score costs from $0.60 to $10.00 per pull since 2022—have triggered a regulatory and competitive backlash that is ending its decades-long monopoly in favor of a duopoly with the lower-cost VantageScore.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
FICO’s aggressive price hikes—increasing mortgage credit score costs from $0.60 to $10.00 per pull since 2022—have triggered a regulatory and competitive backlash that is ending its decades-long monopoly in favor of a duopoly with the lower-cost VantageScore.

## The Collapse of the FICO Monopoly
*   **Aggressive Pricing:** Since 2022, FICO has implemented a 16x price increase in the mortgage vertical, moving from approximately $0.60 per score pull to $10.00. 
    *   **The "Performance Model":** FICO is attempting to transition to a back-end loaded model ($4.95 upfront plus a $33–$65 "success fee" upon loan closing), which averages out to roughly $12.00 per pull.
*   **Regulatory Shift:** The Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), under new Director Bill Pulte, has pivoted from requiring two scores to allowing lenders to choose between FICO and VantageScore.
    *   **Lender Adoption:** Twenty-one major lenders (including Rocket Mortgage and PennyMac), representing a significant portion of the market, have already been approved for a pilot program to use VantageScore.
*   **The Bureau Conflict:** FICO’s "FICO Direct" program attempted to bypass credit bureaus (Equifax, TransUnion, and Experian). In response, the bureaus—who own VantageScore—now often sell FICO scores at 0% margin, giving them a massive incentive to migrate lenders to VantageScore.

## VantageScore: The Emerging Competitor
*   **Cost Advantage:** VantageScore 4.0 is priced at approximately $1.00 per pull, a fraction of FICO’s $10.00+ cost.
*   **Market Expansion:** VantageScore claims to score a larger share of the population, particularly "thin-file" consumers and first-time homebuyers who may not have a traditional FICO score.
*   **Secondary Market Acceptance:** While FICO argues that Mortgage-Backed Security (MBS) investors demand FICO scores, industry feedback suggests investors care about the *risk band* (e.g., 700 vs. 600) rather than the specific brand of the score, as long as the data is translatable.

## Sector Outlook: Financial Information Services
*   **MSCI (Top Pick):** Kelsey Zhu identifies MSCI as a top long pick for 2025. Despite a slowdown in the ESG narrative and exposure to a weak European market, the company maintains a "legendary" management team and a dominant position in indexing.
*   **Verisk:** This insurance data provider is viewed as highly defensible. Its "loss-cost" data is essentially a monopoly, and the P&C insurance industry is more conservative and relationship-driven than the mortgage sector, making it harder to disrupt.
*   **FactSet:** Facing headwinds from the broader shift of active-to-passive investing and a downturn in investment banking "seats," FactSet remains a strong workflow tool but faces more skepticism regarding AI disruption than its peers.

## The Role of AI: Threat vs. Opportunity
*   **Productivity Gains:** While the market narrative focuses on AI disrupting data incumbents, Zhu argues AI provides a "meaningful productivity uplift" for developers, which can be reinvested into margins or new products.
*   **Incumbent Defense:** Established players like Verisk have been utilizing machine learning for a decade. Their vast proprietary "contributory networks" (where lenders/insurers provide data to get data back) remain difficult for AI startups to replicate.
*   **Investment Timing:** Steve Eisman notes that the market is currently in a "narrative-driven" phase regarding AI, where stocks move on sentiment because concrete data on AI’s long-term impact on earnings may not be clear for 12–24 months.

## Notable Quotes

> "FICO had done what other monopolies in the information services coverage have done in general, which is inflation plus 10%... it doesn't really raise any attention. 1600% does get a lot of people's attention." — **Kelsey Zhu**

> "FICO has no product without the credit bureaus, and yet it has angered the credit bureaus who are now incentivized to destroy FICO." — **Steve Eisman**

> "The brand of credit scores is probably a factor that matters the least [to MBS investors]. The band of that credit score does matter... but the difference between the two scores is not important." — **Kelsey Zhu**

> "I've never seen a group that goes down on good news, bad news, and mediocre news... my view is that we're not going to have any real clarity about the impact of AI for at least a year." — **Steve Eisman**

briefings.title: Gautam Adani at CII Annual Business Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: In the 21st century, national sovereignty is defined by the "new geometry of power"—the twin foundations of energy security and digital intelligence.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
In the 21st century, national sovereignty is defined by the "new geometry of power"—the twin foundations of energy security and digital intelligence. To ensure true independence, India must transition from being a service provider for foreign platforms to owning the energy, compute, and data infrastructure that drives its future.

## The Fractured Global Reality
*   **The End of the "Flat World":** Gautam Adani argues that the era of open, borderless supply chains and technology is over. The world is now fractured, with energy, data, and semiconductors treated as instruments of statecraft.
*   **The New Geometry of Power:** National power is no longer just political; it is built on two inseparable dimensions:
    *   **Energy Security:** The country that controls its energy drives its industrial future.
    *   **Digital Intelligence:** The country that controls its compute capacity drives its intelligence future.
*   **Global Precedents:** 
    *   **United States:** Transformed from import-dependent to an energy exporter via the shale revolution and is now negotiating for global compute dominance.
    *   **China:** Built massive industrial scale through a mix of coal and record-breaking renewable installations (440 GW in 2025) while pursuing "AI sovereignty" to avoid reliance on foreign models.

## India’s "Compounding Acceleration"
*   **Economic Velocity:** India took 67 years to reach a $2 trillion GDP, but only 12 years to add the next $2 trillion. Adani predicts India will add the equivalent of a "new European economy" to its GDP every decade.
*   **Energy Milestones:** 
    *   As of March 2026, India surpassed **500 GW** of installed power capacity.
    *   The goal is to reach **2,000 GW by 2047**, representing a massive nation-scale execution of industrialization and decarbonization.
*   **Demand-Led Growth:** Unlike other nations building for abstract futures, India’s advantage is that every unit of capacity built already has a waiting, rising market of consumers and businesses.

## The Three-Layer AI Stack
Adani redefines AI not as mere software, but as physical infrastructure. He outlines a three-tier "AI Stack" that India must own:
*   **The Power Layer:** Reliable, scalable energy is the prerequisite for all digital processing.
*   **The Compute Layer:** The "factories" of the intelligence age, including data centers, GPUs, and cooling systems.
*   **The Application Layer:** Where AI reaches the end-user (farmers, doctors, small businesses) to expand productivity rather than eliminate jobs.
*   **Evolution of the IT Model:** Adani calls for a shift from the "Old IT Model" (writing code for foreign platforms) to a "New Model" where India owns the data, the models, and the platforms.

## Adani Group Strategic Commitments
The Adani Group is positioning itself as the builder of India’s "AI spine" through three foundational investments:
*   **Energy Transition:** A **$100 billion** commitment to clean energy, including the world’s largest single-site renewable plant (30 GW) at Khavda, Gujarat.
*   **Sovereign Compute:** A separate **$100 billion** commitment to the data center business, including a gigawatt-scale campus in Visakhapatnam in partnership with Google.
*   **Human Capital:** A **₹60,000 crore** commitment via the Adani Foundation for education and AI-integrated skilling to ensure the workforce can manage the physical infrastructure of the digital world.

## Notable Quotes
> "If 1947 was about our political freedom, true independence in the 21st century will mean owning the energy that lights our homes and the intelligence that guides our minds." — **Gautam Adani, Chairman of Adani Group**

> "India must not import fear from the Western world. A country can limit its own future not only by lack of capability but also by accepting someone else's assumptions as truth." — **Gautam Adani, Chairman of Adani Group**

> "The future does not come to you. It is built by you." — **Gautam Adani, Chairman of Adani Group**

briefings.title: How AWS Sold Cloud to the CIA – Teresa Carlson GCI
briefings.tldr: Teresa Carlson detail's her journey scaling AWS’s public sector business from zero to $10 billion, highlighting how the landmark CIA cloud contract validated the industry, and explains her current mission at the General Catalyst Institute to bridge the gap between AI startups and global policy frameworks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Teresa Carlson detail's her journey scaling AWS’s public sector business from zero to $10 billion, highlighting how the landmark CIA cloud contract validated the industry, and explains her current mission at the General Catalyst Institute to bridge the gap between AI startups and global policy frameworks.

## The AWS Blueprint: Scaling Public Sector Cloud
* **The CIA "Shot Heard Around the World":** Landing the 2012/2013 CIA contract was the pivotal moment for AWS. It signaled to the commercial world that if the intelligence community could trust the cloud, any enterprise could.
    * This contract required a massive culture shift at Amazon, including building SCIFs and clearing personnel for classified work.
* **Creating a New Industry:** When Carlson started in 2010, there was no mechanism for governments to buy cloud. Her team worked with NIST and GSA to define cloud computing and create the **FedRAMP** security model, which is now the gold standard for regulated industries like finance and healthcare.
* **The Mission-First Sales Model:** Unlike the transactional licensing model at Microsoft, AWS sales were usage-based.
    * Carlson hired "consultative" leaders who focused on solving a customer's mission (e.g., NASA’s Mars Rover data storage) rather than just selling a "widget."

## Amazon Leadership and Decision Frameworks
* **The Death of PowerPoint:** Amazon famously banned PowerPoints in favor of 6-page written narratives. This forced leaders to be prolific writers and storytellers who could describe risks and outcomes with precision.
* **One-Way vs. Two-Way Doors:** Carlson applied Jeff Bezos’s decision-making philosophy to government contracting.
    * **One-way doors:** Irreversible, high-stakes decisions that require deep analysis.
    * **Two-way doors:** Reversible decisions where speed is prioritized over perfect data.
* **Ownership and Detail:** Leaders were expected to be "General Managers" who understood every detail of their P&L, from technical capacity planning to the specific nuances of government contracting.

## Navigating the AI Transformation
* **Hyper-Scale Realities:** Carlson describes the current AI cycle as a "double or triple strap-in" compared to the cloud era. The pace of adoption is far outstripping the creation of regulatory frameworks.
* **The Optimization Point:** Similar to the early days of cloud, Carlson predicts that current massive AI spending will eventually hit an "optimization point." 
    * Customers will move from high-spend experimentation to focusing on specific high-value workloads and token efficiency.
* **The Need for Federal Frameworks:** Carlson advocates for a unified federal AI framework to avoid a "patchwork" of state and international regulations that could stifle startup growth.

## The General Catalyst Institute: Bridging VC and DC
* **Advocating for the "Unfair Advantage":** Small startups lack the lobbying budgets of Big Tech. The Institute focuses on educating policymakers about how startup technology (like agentic AI in healthcare) can solve national problems.
* **DC Etiquette for Tech Founders:** Carlson coaches founders on how to approach Washington with "solution orientation" rather than just identifying problems.
    * **Legitimacy via Professionalism:** She emphasizes the importance of "showing up serious"—dressing professionally and showing respect for the gravity of government work to gain trust from lawmakers.
* **Global Resilience:** The Institute works across highly regulated sectors including defense, healthcare, and energy to ensure startups have the policy tailwinds needed to compete globally, particularly against China.

## Notable Quotes

> "I used to tell my team at AWS strap in cause you won't see anything like this and with AI I'm like this is a double or triple strap in. It's like nuts." — **Teresa Carlson**

> "We won a contract in 2012, 2013 with the Central Intelligence Agency and it really was kind of the shot heard around the world because commercial enterprises were like: 'What? If the Central Intelligence Agency can use cloud, we can use cloud.'" — **Teresa Carlson**

> "Our philosophy is we want to be solution providers, not problem identifiers. That makes a huge tone difference if we go in with 'we want to be helpful.'" — **Teresa Carlson**

> "If you really want to be taken seriously [in DC], you need to show up looking serious with them because they have a lot of people coming at them." — **Teresa Carlson**

briefings.title: How She Got Peter Thiel to Anchor Her First Fund (Without Pitching Him)
briefings.tldr: Keri Findley, founder of Tacora Capital, leverages a "ratings arbitrage" strategy to invest in highly illiquid credit assets that traditional institutions cannot hold, generating alpha by solving complex financing problems for venture-backed startups.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Keri Findley, founder of Tacora Capital, leverages a "ratings arbitrage" strategy to invest in highly illiquid credit assets that traditional institutions cannot hold, generating alpha by solving complex financing problems for venture-backed startups. Her reputation for rational, "age-adjusted" trading led Peter Thiel to anchor her first fund as his largest investment outside of Founders Fund, based on personal trust and her ability to structure unconventional risks.

## The Investment Philosophy: Risk vs. Illiquidity
*   **The Illiquidity Spectrum:** Findley differentiates her strategy by moving along the illiquidity spectrum rather than the risk spectrum. She targets assets that lack the ratings required by insurance companies or the liquidity needed by mutual funds.
*   **Ratings Arbitrage:** A core strategy involves "finding, creating, and analyzing" assets that the market misprices due to regulatory constraints.
    *   **2009 Mortgage Bond Case:** Findley bought triple-A bonds downgraded to "D" (default) for 60 cents on the dollar. By restructuring them into trusts, she could get 60% of the bond re-rated as "single-A" to sell to mutual funds at 95 cents, effectively acquiring the remaining high-yield "mez" bonds for nearly nothing.
*   **The Advantage of "No Scars":** Findley attributes her early success at Third Point to being a young trader during the 2008 crisis. Lacking the "battle scars" and emotional trauma of older traders, she could rationally analyze data (e.g., that 97% of mortgage defaults occur by month 60) to identify "fulcrum securities" others were too terrified to touch.

## Strategic Operations at Tacora Capital
*   **The "North Star" Portfolio:** Tacora maintains a diversified split across three primary sectors:
    *   **PropTech (1/3):** Real estate-related credit.
    *   **InsurTech (1/3):** Statutory capital and surplus notes for niche insurance products with low loss ratios.
    *   **FinTech (1/3):** Financial services, invoice purchasing, and receivables finance.
*   **Solving the Scaling Problem:** Tacora focuses on deals in the **$30 million range**, a "sweet spot" where they face less competition. Larger private credit firms (Ares, Apollo, Blackstone) have scaled so much they now require $150M+ deal sizes to move the needle, leaving the mid-market underserved.
*   **Venture Debt Alternative:** Tacora provides an alternative to dilutive equity. Instead of a Series A company giving away 20-30% of the business to fund a lending product, Tacora provides the warehouse line in exchange for a small equity piece (warrants) and interest.

## Relationship-Based Fundraising and the "Thiel Anchor"
*   **The Peter Thiel Partnership:** Findley secured Thiel as her anchor investor without a formal pitch. After building trust over several years through discussions on ideas and lending, Thiel offered to be her biggest investor, stating he was comfortable being the *only* investor if necessary.
*   **The Power of Trust:** Findley notes that Thiel invests more in the person and their ambition than the specific asset class. His family office’s proximity to her early work with SoFi allowed him to observe her "stewardship of capital" firsthand.
*   **Institutional Constraints:** Despite a stellar track record at Third Point, Findley found raising a first-time credit fund exceptionally difficult due to the high "quantum of capital" required to achieve necessary portfolio diversity (at least $100M+ to start).

## Risk Management and Counterparty Ethics
*   **Avoiding Hard Assets:** A key lesson from Fund 1 was to **never fund mobile equipment** (e.g., tractors, trucks). Findley discovered that when a company fails, physical assets in rural areas are easily stolen or hidden by disgruntled employees. She now focuses exclusively on financial assets like insurance notes and invoices.
*   **The "Ethical Counterparty" Rule:** Findley argues that credit "brings out the worst in people" during defaults. She prioritizes working with founders who have ethical VC board members (e.g., Andreessen Horowitz), as these VCs act as a "golden ticket" to ensure the company behaves professionally during restructuring to protect their own reputations.
*   **Portfolio Expectations:** Tacora constructs portfolios with roughly **15-21 deals**, expecting approximately one-third to wind down or default. The goal is to ensure the equity upside from the successful "winners" (which can return 9 or 10 figures) offsets any credit losses.

## Notable Quotes
> "I always liked assets that were perceived to be risky, but I never thought they were as risky—I just thought they were very illiquid... usually, a mutual fund can't buy them, and banks can't own them." — **Keri Findley**

> "I could work out the worst deal I’ve ever done with an honest, good person on the other side, but I would have trouble working out the best deal I’ve ever done with a less ethical character." — **Keri Findley**

> "The size of a company is directly proportional to the problem that it's solving... The funds that actually solve problems are the funds that have embedded alpha." — **David Weisburd**

> "There's just no need to focus on these things that you think are going to validate you... just keep doing you, taking your own path, working hard, being ethical, and everything will eventually fall into place." — **Keri Findley**

briefings.title: James Gorman - Chairman Emeritus of Morgan Stanley  | Investment Conference 2026

people.name: James Gorman
people.role: Chairman, The Walt Disney Co. and Chairman Emeritus, Morgan Stanley

briefings.tldr: Effective leadership requires a "strategy-first" approach where business success earns the right to build culture, supported by a transition from employee "tenancy" to institutional "landlordship" and transparent, rigorous succession planning.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Effective leadership requires a "strategy-first" approach where business success earns the right to build culture, supported by a transition from employee "tenancy" to institutional "landlordship" and transparent, rigorous succession planning.

## The Sequence of Strategy, Culture, and "Winning"
James Gorman argues that corporate culture cannot be established in a vacuum; it must be preceded by a viable business model.

*   **Strategy as a Prerequisite:** Strategy earns a leader the right to talk about culture. It is difficult to preach values to employees if the business is failing or if layoffs are imminent.
*   **The "Winning" Catalyst:** Nothing drives culture more effectively than winning. 
    *   High-performing employees ("goers") need to know they are part of a winning organization to remain motivated.
    *   Winning creates an infectious environment where people are willing to do exceptional things.
*   **The Reinvention Cycle:** Gorman views a company's longevity as a series of train cabins: strategy, then culture, then a new strategy, then culture. Strong cultural "bones" provide the confidence needed to reinvent the business over decades.

## From "Tenants" to "Landlords"
A central "Gormanism" involves shifting the mindset of employees—particularly in high-finance—away from short-term personal gain toward institutional health.

*   **Institutional Loyalty:** Employees should stop acting like "tenants" looking for their next bonus and start acting like "landlords" of the institution.
*   **The 50/50 Brain Test:** Gorman advocates for a balance where an employee is 50% driven by personal ego/confidence and 50% driven by the institution’s success.
    *   A culture dominated by individual pieces (98% self-interest) results in a "war of attrition" that damages the firm.
    *   Alignment is reinforced by stock-based compensation, where personal wealth is tied to the firm's long-term performance.

## Mentorship and the Return to Office
Gorman remains a staunch advocate for physical office presence, viewing it as a moral and professional obligation for senior leaders.

*   **The Mentoring Gap:** Young employees are "nuts" to stay home because they miss the soft cues and mentorship that occur in person.
*   **Senior Responsibility:** Senior leaders have an obligation to be present to develop the next generation, just as they were once mentored.
*   **The "Restaurant" Standard:** During the pandemic, Gorman famously argued that if employees were comfortable going out to restaurants or gyms, they should be comfortable returning to the office. 
    *   He noted the inequity of senior leaders working from comfortable homes while junior staff struggled in cramped, shared apartments with no privacy.

## Best Practices in Succession Planning
Drawing from his experiences at Morgan Stanley and Disney, Gorman outlines a rigorous framework for leadership transition.

*   **The Three Pillars:** Success requires **Clarity, Transparency, and Intentionality.** 
    *   **Transparency of Process:** Use a formal succession committee with clear start, transition, and finish dates.
    *   **Total Respect:** Internal candidates should be told they are being considered and given the opportunity to opt-out if they find the process too rigorous.
*   **Rigorous Testing:** At Morgan Stanley, Gorman required candidates to write strategy papers on short notice and undergo intensive Q&A to ensure the ideas were their own.
*   **The "Clean" Break:** Gorman emphasizes that the "old king" must truly leave for the "new king" to succeed. Once the transition period ends, the former CEO should not "hang around the hoop."
*   **Disney Succession:** Gorman confirmed that **Josh D’Amaro** was the board’s choice for the new CEO after a rigorous process that evaluated both internal and external candidates. He noted the board successfully retained the internal candidates who were not selected.

## The Role of the Board and CEO Peer Support
Gorman touched on the loneliness of the CEO role and the boundaries of board governance.

*   **CEO Outreach:** Gorman makes a point of calling every new Fortune 500 CEO to offer a "therapy" line for non-business issues like activist investors, board dysfunction, or personal family stress.
*   **Advisory vs. Execution:** Regarding high-profile controversies (e.g., political demands regarding ABC/Jimmy Kimmel), Gorman noted that a director's role is to **advise, not do.** The CEO and their team must make the final decisions, as they are the ones who must live with the consequences.

> "Strategy earns you the right to talk about culture. It’s very hard to talk about culture if the business isn’t working." — **James Gorman**

> "Young people are nuts if they're not in the office; that’s where mentoring happens." — **James Gorman**

> "The king has to be dead for the new king to succeed. Your job is to take the ship from one port to another, not to take over the ship only for yourself." — **James Gorman**

briefings.title: Roundhill's DRAM ETF notches $6B on memory demand, here’s their next big idea
briefings.tldr: The massive surge in Roundhill’s Memory ETF (DRAM) highlights that memory chips have replaced processors as the primary bottleneck in the AI buildout, shifting the sector from a cyclical consumer-driven industry to a high-growth secular powerhouse.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The massive surge in Roundhill’s Memory ETF (DRAM) highlights that memory chips have replaced processors as the primary bottleneck in the AI buildout, shifting the sector from a cyclical consumer-driven industry to a high-growth secular powerhouse.

## The Memory Bottleneck and Structural Shift
*   **Supply-Demand Imbalance:** The current shortage in high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and DRAM is expected to persist through 2026–2028 due to the three-to-five-year lead time required to build new fabrication plants.
*   **End of Cyclicality:** Historically, memory was a "boom and bust" industry driven by consumer electronics (phones, TVs).
    *   **Data Center Dominance:** Micron’s revenue share from data centers has jumped from 15% to 65% in just a few years.
    *   **Contract Stability:** Short-term consumer contracts are being replaced by long-term data center agreements, leading to a "re-rating" of the sector's valuation.
*   **The "Vera Rubin" Effect:** Newer generations of AI chips (like Nvidia's upcoming Rubin architecture) require significantly more memory than current Blackwell chips, further tightening supply.

## Earnings Momentum and Valuations
*   **Earnings-Backed Growth:** Despite triple-digit price increases in names like Micron, the rally is supported by massive upward earnings revisions.
    *   **Reasonable Pricing:** Analysts suggest that while prices are up 300%, earnings expectations for some firms have risen six-to-eightfold, making current multiples appear reasonable.
    *   **S&P 500 Impact:** Micron alone has contributed approximately $5 to the S&P 500’s earnings growth this year.
*   **International Opportunities:** The "narrowing" of the AI trade outside the U.S. points toward South Korea (Kospi) and Taiwan as the primary beneficiaries of the memory and semiconductor demand.

## The "AI Value Chain" and Secondary Plays
*   **Industrial Enablers:** Beyond chips, the "back-end" of data center construction offers significant opportunities.
    *   **Infrastructure:** Companies providing concrete, plumbing, and electrical work for data centers currently possess high pricing power and improved efficiency.
*   **Optical and Photonics:** For semiconductor chips to function effectively in clusters, high-speed communication is required.
    *   **Key Players:** Roundhill’s Generative AI ETF (CHAT) identifies companies like Credo, Coherent, and Lumentum as essential for chip-to-chip communication.
*   **The Defensive Rotation:** Mega-cap growth (the "Mag Seven") is increasingly viewed as a defensive "safe haven" during periods of macroeconomic uncertainty or high oil prices.

## Macroeconomic Risks and Geopolitical Hedges
*   **Geopolitical Insulation:** While global conflicts (Iran, Ukraine) create volatility, U.S. large-cap growth remains relatively insulated compared to Europe. 
*   **Energy vs. Technology:** Experts suggest buying oil as a tail-risk commodity hedge, but emphasize that mega-cap tech is fundamentally driven by silicon rather than energy costs.
*   **Sustained Demand:** AI and data center buildouts are now significant contributors to U.S. GDP, suggesting that demand may remain resilient despite broader economic cooling.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "Investors are waking up to the fact that the biggest bottleneck in the AI buildout is actually memory chips... we’re seeing expectations for this supply and demand imbalance not just to extend into 2026, but perhaps to 2027, even to 2028." 
— **Dave Mazza**, CEO, Roundhill Investments

> "We don’t like price momentum unless it has earnings momentum... if we’re up 300% but your earnings expectations are up six to eightfold for the next few years, it still comes back reasonably priced to us." 
— **Drew Pettit**, Director of U.S. Equity Strategy, Citi

> "Mega-cap tech runs on chips, it doesn't run on oil." 
— **Dave Mazza**, CEO, Roundhill Investments

briefings.title: The Golden Age Thesis | Marc Andreessen on MTS
briefings.tldr: We are entering a "Golden Age" of productivity where AI acts as a superpower for "builders," enabling a 20x increase in output that will likely expand the economy and job market rather than shrink it, despite institutional fear campaigns and historical corporate bloat.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** We are entering a "Golden Age" of productivity where AI acts as a superpower for "builders," enabling a 20x increase in output that will likely expand the economy and job market rather than shrink it, despite institutional fear campaigns and historical corporate bloat.

## The AI Productivity Revolution & the Rise of the "Builder"
* **The "AI Vampire" Phenomenon:** Marc Andreessen describes a new class of workers who are exhausted but euphoric because their marginal productivity has exploded.
    * **Programmer Gains:** Leading-edge programmers are seeing up to a **20x increase** in productivity compared to just one year ago.
    * **Shift in Roles:** The traditional silos of programmer, designer, and product manager are merging into a single role: the **"Builder."** AI allows one person to execute the functions of all three disciplines.
* **Marginal Productivity vs. Job Loss:** Andreessen argues that increasing worker productivity does not lead to fewer jobs; historically, it leads to an expansion of work, higher demand for talent, and higher compensation.
* **AI-Native Success:** Contrary to "doomer" narratives that junior roles will vanish, Andreessen suggests companies will prioritize hiring "AI-native" youth (ages 15-25) who can outperform veteran "Luddite" peers.

## Corporate Bloat & the "Twitter Proof"
* **The Scale of Inefficiency:** Most Silicon Valley companies are estimated to be **2x to 8x bloated**.
    * **The Elon Musk Model:** Twitter (X) successfully cut approximately **70-90% of its staff** while maintaining or improving performance, serving as a forecast for the broader industry.
* **AI as a Scapegoat:** Andreessen suggests many current tech layoffs are not caused by AI, but rather companies using AI as a "scapegoat" to finally trim decades of accumulated organizational bloat.
* **Non-Profit Inefficiency:** The bloat extends to NGOs and government-adjacent organizations, which often prioritize self-aggrandizement and power over their stated missions.

## Institutional Authority & the SPLC Controversy
* **The SPLC Indictment:** Andreessen highlights a DOJ indictment alleging the Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) used donor funds to secretly fund extreme groups like the KKK and the American Nazi Party.
    * **Creating the Boogeyman:** The theory is that if an organization's purpose is to fight an enemy, they have a financial incentive to ensure that enemy exists.
* **"Suicidal Empathy":** A concept discussed via Gad Saad, describing social reform movements that claim compassion but result in self-destructiveness or harm to the communities they represent (e.g., San Francisco's "harm reduction" policies).
* **Deplatforming Power:** For years, the SPLC acted as an "outsourced US Department of Racism Detection," wielding unchecked power to debank and censor individuals without government oversight.

## The Epistemological Divide: Boomers vs. Zoomers
* **"Boomer Truth":** The older generation is characterized by a reliance on legacy media (TV, New York Times) and a belief in institutional authority.
* **Zoomer Skepticism:** Gen Z is described as "post-truth" and highly skeptical of authority figures, largely due to their experiences with COVID-19 policies and "woke" cultural shifts.
    * **Psychological Warfare Awareness:** Younger generations are more sensitive to the fact that they are targets of psychological warfare and media manipulation.
* **Advice for New Graduates:** Andreessen advises the 18–22 age cohort to "gain AI superpowers" immediately. Those who lean into the technology will become "super producers" in a way that previous generations cannot match.

## Public Sentiment vs. Real-World Behavior
* **"Project Fear":** While media polls show low public sentiment toward AI, actual usage data (NPS and retention) is record-breaking. 
    * **The "Ice Cream" Paradox:** People may tell pollsters they fear AI or think it's bad for society, but their behavior shows they find it indispensable and high-utility.
* **AI Cope:** Andreessen identifies "AI Cope" as the tendency of skeptics to dismiss any positive AI experience as "AI Psychosis" or delusion, despite the technology’s rapidly increasing reasoning and coding capabilities.

> "We are going to see super producers, the likes of which we've never seen in the world. It’s the most dramatic increase in programmer productivity in ever." — **Marc Andreessen**

> "Twitter proved it... cutting 70% and then it's running better or as good as it was before. [Elon Musk] has really forecasted the future through his own actions." — **Marc Andreessen**

> "If your group's entire purpose for existing is to fight an enemy, then you need to make sure that that enemy exists. To do that, of course, you would fund them." — **Marc Andreessen**
